steps.title: Torrontés
steps.body: Torrontés Riojano, a cross of Muscat of Alexandria and Criolla Chica, is Argentina's own white grape and Salta's signature. In Cafayate, it gives intensely floral, aromatic wines with rose, jasmine, orange blossom and peach, yet usually dry, with fresh acidity. Altitude helps it keep acidity and avoid bitterness.

steps.title: Reds
steps.body: Malbec and Cabernet Sauvignon thrive too. Intense UV light thickens skins, giving very deep colour, firm tannins and concentrated dark fruit, often with spice and herbs. Tannat also does well. Salta's reds are bold and intense, quite different from Mendoza's.

steps.explanation: Salta's grapes are shaped by altitude.

steps.body: Torrontés smells sweet, but taste it: most are dry. That contrast is part of its charm.

steps.prompt: Why are Salta's reds so deeply coloured?
steps.explanation: Grapes protect themselves with thicker, darker skins.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Torrontés is Salta's floral, dry signature white
Malbec and Cabernet give dark, intense reds
Altitude and UV light shape both
